readme:
# JobMail Jobs Scraper

Scrape job ads from JobMail ([jobmail.co.za](https://www.jobmail.co.za/)), a job board in South Africa. You get the title, company or recruiter, location, salary range, posting date, industry and listing type for every job. Turn on job details to add the full description, reference number, closing date, province, company page and apply link. Search by keyword and narrow it by industry, location, job type, poster type and date posted.

## What you get

- One row per job, with parsed salary numbers in rand where the job shows a salary range.
- Posted dates as ISO 8601 dates, and the exact time with job details.
- Optional job page fields: description (HTML and text), reference number, closing date, province, industry and sub-industry names, company page and apply link.
- Each job once per run, even when several keywords find it.
- A run with no input returns 5 jobs for the keyword accountant.

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

`https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/jobmail-jobs-scraper`

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `jobmail-jobs-scraper` to find up to 5 jobs for the keyword "accountant" (accountant roles in Cape Town). Return results as a table with title, company, location and job URL."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) receive the full input schema automatically.

## Input

Every field is optional. Example:

```json
{
  "includeDetails": false,
  "maxResults": 5,
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 5,
  "searchQueries": [
    "accountant"
  ]
}
```

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | Keywords such as accountant, driver or software developer. Each keyword is its own search. Empty means the newest jobs. |
| `location` | One province, city or suburb, for example Gauteng, Cape Town or Durban. Empty means all of South Africa. |
| `industry` | One industry, for example it-computer, finance-accounting or retail. Any means all. |
| `jobType` | Full time only, or any. |
| `posterType` | Jobs posted by employers, by recruiters, or both. |
| `datePosted` | Jobs posted in the last 2, 7 or 14 days, or any time. |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | Jobs per keyword. Default 50, up to 1000. |
| `maxResults` | Jobs in total. Default 200. 0 means no limit. |
| `includeDetails` | Read each job page for the extra fields. Default false. |

## Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Vacancy id of the job ad. It is the dedup key. |
| `title` | string | Job title as shown on the listing. |
| `company` | string, null | Name of the employer or recruiter that posted the job. |
| `company_id` | string, null | Id of the poster profile on JobMail. Needs includeDetails. |
| `company_url` | string, null | Address of the poster profile on JobMail. Needs includeDetails. |
| `poster_type` | string, null | Who posted the job, as the site shows it: Employer or Recruiter. |
| `location` | string, null | Suburb, city or province of the job, as shown on the listing. |
| `province` | string, null | Province of the job. Needs includeDetails. |
| `country` | string, null | Country code of the job. Needs includeDetails. |
| `industry_slug` | string, null | Industry of the job as the site writes it in the address. |
| `sub_industry_slug` | string, null | Sub-industry of the job as the site writes it in the address. |
| `industry` | string, null | Industry name. Needs includeDetails. |
| `sub_industry` | string, null | Sub-industry name. Needs includeDetails. |
| `salary_text` | string, null | Salary as shown on the listing, for example 'R18 000,00 - R24 000,00' or 'Market Related'. |
| `salary_min` | number, null | Lower end of the salary in rand. Null when the listing shows no figure. |
| `salary_max` | number, null | Upper end of the salary in rand. Null when the listing shows no figure. |
| `salary_currency` | string, null | ZAR when the listing shows a figure. |
| `salary_period` | string, null | month, year, hour, day or week, as the listing states it. Null when there is no figure. |
| `job_type` | string, null | Job type as shown on the job page, for example FULL TIME. Needs includeDetails. |
| `employment_type` | string, null | Employment type of the job page data, for example FULL_TIME. Needs includeDetails. |
| `listing_type` | string, null | How the listing is marked: verified, premium or sponsored. |
| `badges` | array | Marks on the listing card: Verified, Premium or Sponsored. |
| `apply_external` | boolean | true when the apply button of the card leads to the poster's own site. |
| `posted_text` | string, null | Posting date as written on the listing. |
| `date_posted` | string, null | Posting date. A date (YYYY-MM-DD) from the listing, or the exact time in ISO 8601 UTC with includeDetails. |
| `valid_through` | string, null | Date the job ad runs until, ISO 8601 UTC. Needs includeDetails. |
| `reference_number` | string, null | Reference number of the job ad. Needs includeDetails. |
| `apply_url` | string, null | Address the job page gives for applying on the poster's site. Needs includeDetails. |
| `description_html` | string, null | Job description with its HTML. Needs includeDetails. |
| `description_text` | string, null | Job description as plain text. Needs includeDetails. |
| `job_url` | string | Full address of the job page. |
| `details_fetched` | boolean | true when the job page was read. The columns marked 'Needs includeDetails' are filled only then. |
| `search_query` | string | The keyword that found the job, or 'all jobs' when none was set. |
| `source` | string | Always jobmail.co.za. |
| `scraped_at` | string | When the row was scraped, ISO 8601 UTC. |

Fields that a job does not show are `null`, and lists are empty. The columns marked "Needs includeDetails." stay `null` while `includeDetails` is off.

## Pricing

This Actor uses pay per event. There is a small `apify-actor-start` event when a run starts and one `job-result` event for each job in the dataset. You are never charged for a job twice, and a run stops when it reaches the maximum charge you set.

Price: $0.001 start fee per run, then $0.0009 per job result ($0.90 per 1,000 jobs).

## FAQ

**Which filters can I combine?**
All of them: keyword, industry, location, job type, poster type and date posted. With several keywords, every keyword runs as its own search with the same filters. A filter value that matches nothing returns 0 jobs, it is never ignored.

**Why is the salary empty for many jobs?**
Many posters write "Market Related" or "Negotiable" instead of a number. Then `salary_text` says so and `salary_min` and `salary_max` are `null`.

**Why can the poster type filter be slow?**
JobMail has no address for it, so the Actor reads result pages and keeps the jobs of the poster type you chose. A rare poster type can take many pages.

**What happens when a keyword finds nothing?**
The run ends normally with the status "0 jobs found for <keyword>." and nothing is charged. JobMail then shows its latest jobs on the page, and the Actor does not return them.
